CBC.text: A complete blood count assesses red cells, white cells and platelets. These measurements support evaluation of anemia, infection and other blood disorders. Interpret cell counts and indices together with clinical findings and, when indicated, a peripheral blood smear. A three-part analyzer differential reports grouped white-cell populations.

LFT.text: Liver tests assess a pattern of enzymes, bilirubin and proteins associated with liver and biliary function. An isolated abnormal result does not establish a diagnosis. Interpret the complete pattern with symptoms, medication history and other investigations; some markers may also be affected by conditions outside the liver.

KFT.text: Kidney investigations assess waste-product clearance and, when included, electrolyte balance. Creatinine and urea results should be interpreted with clinical findings and other kidney tests. Reference intervals apply to the reported specimen, unit and laboratory method; a value within the interval does not by itself exclude kidney disease.

WIDAL.text: The Widal test measures agglutinating antibodies to Salmonella antigens. A single titre cannot reliably confirm or exclude enteric fever. False-positive results limit its diagnostic value; CDC guidance does not recommend Widal serology for diagnosis. Interpret any reported titre with the clinical assessment and appropriate culture-based investigations.

VIRAL.text: Viral-marker panels contain separate antigen or antibody tests. Each result must be interpreted according to the specific marker, exposure history and interval since exposure. A reactive screening result may require additional testing; a nonreactive result during an early window period may not exclude infection.

VITD.text: Vitamin D supports calcium absorption and bone health. Circulating 25-hydroxyvitamin D is commonly measured to assess vitamin D status. Interpretation depends on the assay and clinical context. Confirm whether the assay measures total D2 plus D3; this is different from measurement of 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D.

VITB12.text: Vitamin B12 supports red-cell production and normal nervous-system function. Measurement helps assess possible deficiency. Interpret the result with symptoms, blood-count findings and the clinical history; a serum concentration alone may not fully establish the cause of a suspected deficiency.

BHCG.text: Human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) is measured in blood to support assessment of pregnancy and selected other clinical conditions. A single concentration does not establish pregnancy location or viability. Interpretation may require serial measurements, clinical assessment and imaging, depending on the indication.

UPT.text: A urine pregnancy test detects hCG above the assay's detection threshold. Testing very early or using dilute urine may produce a negative result despite pregnancy. If the result and clinical findings disagree, further testing may be needed according to the treating clinician's assessment.

URINE.text: Routine urinalysis combines physical examination, chemical testing and microscopy where performed. Findings can support assessment of urinary, kidney and metabolic conditions. Collection quality and specimen handling affect interpretation. Urinalysis findings alone do not identify a causative organism; culture is a separate investigation when indicated.

THYROID.text: Thyroid tests assess circulating thyroid hormones and pituitary thyroid-stimulating hormone. Interpret TSH with the thyroid-hormone results and clinical findings. Total and free T3 or T4 measurements are different tests and use different intervals. Pregnancy, medications and assay interference may affect interpretation.

HBA1C.text: HbA1c reflects average glycemic exposure over approximately two to three months. It is used in diabetes assessment and monitoring. Conditions that change red-cell survival or interfere with the assay can affect the result. Diagnostic interpretation and monitoring targets depend on the clinical context and applicable guidance.

MALARIA.text: Malaria investigations look for evidence of malaria parasites in blood. Microscopy, antigen tests and molecular assays detect different targets. A negative result may not exclude infection when clinical suspicion remains, particularly with low parasite density; additional testing may be required by the treating clinician.

DENGUE.text: Interpret dengue markers according to the time since symptom onset and the assay used. NS1 antigen and molecular tests are used during early illness, while antibody responses develop over time. A negative test does not always exclude dengue. IgG in a single sample should not be used alone to diagnose acute infection.

SEMEN.text: Semen analysis assesses ejaculate characteristics and sperm quantity and quality, including movement and morphology where examined. Collection conditions and biological variation influence results. An individual result does not by itself establish fertility or infertility; interpretation may require repeat specimens and clinical evaluation.

PAP.text: Cervical cytology screens for abnormal cervical-cell changes. Specimen adequacy and the cytological findings should be considered together. An abnormal screening result does not by itself diagnose cancer; follow-up depends on the cytology category, HPV findings where available and the clinical history.

ALLERGY.text: Total IgE measures the overall concentration of immunoglobulin E. It does not identify a specific allergen or establish an allergy diagnosis by itself. Interpret the result with the clinical history and, when appropriate, allergen-specific investigations.

HBSAG.text: Hepatitis B surface antigen is one marker used in the assessment of hepatitis B infection. Interpret it with other hepatitis B markers and the clinical history. Follow the assay's confirmation procedure for a reactive screening result; one marker alone does not fully classify the stage of infection.

HIV.text: HIV screening detects antibodies, antigen or both, depending on the assay. A reactive screen requires supplemental testing under the applicable diagnostic algorithm. A nonreactive result may not exclude recent infection during the assay's window period. Interpret results with exposure timing and clinical assessment.

IRON.text: Iron studies assess circulating iron and its binding or transport characteristics. Interpret serum iron, binding capacity and transferrin saturation together with the blood count and ferritin where available. An isolated result does not establish iron deficiency or overload; clinical context and other findings are necessary.

LIPID.text: A lipid profile assesses cholesterol fractions and triglycerides to support cardiovascular risk assessment. Interpret the results with age, medical history and other risk factors. Clinical treatment goals are not the same as a general laboratory reference interval. Calculated fractions depend on the equation and its applicability.

KFT:URIC.text: Uric acid is produced during the breakdown of purines, which occur naturally in the body and in foods. Much of it is removed through the kidneys. Concentrations can be influenced by production and excretion. Raised uric acid may be associated with gout or uric-acid stones, but the blood result alone does not diagnose these conditions.

KFT:CREAT.text: Creatinine is a waste product related to muscle activity that is cleared from blood by the kidneys. Its concentration contributes to assessment of kidney filtration. Interpret it with the patient's characteristics, other kidney investigations and changes over time.

DENGUE:DENGUE_NS1.text: NS1 is a dengue viral antigen used in assessment of early infection. Interpretation depends on illness timing and the performance of the specific assay; a negative result does not exclude dengue.

DENGUE:DENGUE_IGM.text: Dengue IgM may support evidence of recent infection. Antibody detection depends on illness timing, and cross-reactivity can occur. Interpret with other dengue markers and the clinical findings.

DENGUE:DENGUE_IGG.text: A positive dengue IgG result may reflect previous exposure. IgG in a single specimen is not sufficient to diagnose acute dengue infection.
